response.text: Cedar retains 8 grams of water. This is calculated by subtracting the dry reference mass (40 grams) from the measured mass (48 grams) of Cedar's soil sample. The calculation is shown in the notes: 48 grams - 40 grams = 8 grams [aster-lab.txt Page 1].

cases.question: If other conditions stay the same, what happens when Lumen aperture area decreases?

response.text: When the Lumen aperture area decreases, less light is admitted to the sensor. To compensate for the reduced light, a longer exposure time is needed to collect the same amount of light. This is explained in [lumen-rig.txt Page 1].
response.follow_up: Do you understand how a decrease in aperture area affects the exposure time needed to maintain the same level of light on the sensor?

source_citations.text:
Lumen is a fictional optics rig. An aperture admits light to a sensor. Reducing aperture area admits less light when other conditions stay the same. A longer exposure collects light for more time. The rig's sensor converts collected light into a recorded signal, and a dark frame is collected with the aperture covered. The example notes use the dark frame to identify a background signal.

model, aperture diameter, exposure duration, signal-to-noise measurement, or calibration coefficient is specified. A background signal is a defined concept, not a supplied numerical measurement.
